supportedFacts.claim: Submissions opened 2 Nov 2026; Feb 28 deadline; Mar 15 notification; Pulsant theme; free entry; main >3 min/student >1 min; May 22–23 2027 tentative. Opening is 14 days before report date.

remainingIssues: About-800-word request not met: only 578 whitespace words before Sources.

Original source lists basic submission conditions (AI workflow explanation, subtitles, no resubmissions); omitted in article. This is a practical completeness improvement, not a new mandatory rubric.

article.wordCountNote: No 800-word requirement for N2; length is not marked a failure.

newsroom-2.userScopeEvidence: requester-relays/newsroom-2/user-confirmation.json confirms global framing, concrete tools/versions/study dates, older background allowed, evidence-led conclusion; confirmation came after same assumptions were relayed and is not retroactive evidence of an earlier answer.
newsroom-2.contentVerdict: Complete and improved evidence-date disclosure, includes positive detection evidence, but categorical generalisations and missing actual detector versions prevent treating it as fully publication-ready independent fact-check.

primarySupport.claim: Weber-Wulff tested 12 public + 2 commercial tools and reports poor reliability/obfuscation; explicitly historical 2023 evidence.

Park abstract states 135,389 edited manuscript pairs and FPR range 0.0%–100.0% across 13 detectors, with style as confound; not evidence every detector has 100% error. Revised text adds per-tool/per-corpus qualification.
Liang abstract supports non-native-writing bias and bypass risk for studied 2023 detectors.
Bitton abstract genuinely reports unanimous ensemble precision 0.9988 and FPR 0.0004; article includes this opposing evidence with dataset qualification.
Li watermark abstract supports secret-key statistical detection with controllable false positives.

remainingIssues: Lead and recommendations say detectors are not evidence of authorship and at best a weak signal, which overgeneralises limited, mixed studies. Safer supported conclusion: insufficient as sole or conclusive evidence for an individual student; tools and settings differ.

Article admits no institutional policies or actual assignment tests, yet claims all three subquestions point the same way and makes categorical educational claims. Missing evidence should leave those questions partly open.
Only Turnitin/PlagiarismCheck named through 2023 study; paper version identifiers are present, but actual detector/model versions are absent despite confirmed scope.
Watermark paragraph asserts essentially all student assignments are unwatermarked without supporting prevalence evidence in the fetched abstract.
Social headline AI Detectors Can’t Reliably Tell If a Student Cheated conflates AI authorship with misconduct, which depends on course rules.

Positive ensemble and watermark evidence is included, an improvement over one-sided treatment, but dismissed as best-case without full-paper analysis of coverage/abstention; abstract-only scope limits the synthesis.

reviewCoverage.note: Reviewer openly disclosed reliance on reporter brief. It also read three inherited N1 documents irrelevant to detector checking; not source-body verification.
